display_name: Foxglove Studio (foxglove_bridge — self-hosted teleop console bridge)
misconfig_patterns: foxglove_bridge has NO authentication by default — anyone reaching port 8765 gets full WebSocket subscribe + publish capability
tls / certfile / keyfile launch params add transport encryption but NOT authentication — encrypted-anonymous is still anonymous
No token, password, or API-key parameter exists in the foxglove_bridge launch file as of 2026-06-09
Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: foxglove.websocket.v1 handshake echoes back even before any auth challenge — identity leak before any access decision
Channel-list (/listChannels) enumerates every topic the bridge exposes without subscribing — capability fingerprint leak
advertise + publish messages let a connected client become a new publisher on any topic, including robot control topics
Foxglove Studio (the browser/desktop app) connects to ws://<host>:8765 directly — no client-side authentication enforced
Foxglove Cloud (the paid SaaS at app.foxglove.dev) DOES have OAuth/org auth — but the self-hosted bridge does not inherit that
Common docker-compose pattern: foxglove_bridge published to host port 8765 alongside ros:humble — both reachable
Reverse-proxy guidance is documented but optional; bare bridge on public IP is a frequent pattern in academic + early-startup deployments

active_probe.false_positive_check: WebSocket upgrade response with Sec-WebSocket-Protocol exactly foxglove.websocket.v1 is the unique identity signal — this subprotocol is foxglove-bridge-specific and not used by other websocket services. Reject if subprotocol header is absent (generic websocket) or if it advertises a different protocol (rosbridge-v1.0, mqtt, etc). Secondary confirmation: open the websocket and read first server message — foxglove_bridge sends a serverInfo JSON message with 'name' = 'foxglove_bridge' as the first frame.

shodan_dorks.notes: Foxglove bridge IS directly Shodan-indexable on port 8765 — WebSocket handshake echoes Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: foxglove.websocket.v1 which is the unique fingerprint. Per Insight #93, basic dork has no port: constraint to catch reverse-proxied deployments on 80/443/8080. Body-marker variants of 'foxglove_bridge' also surface bare HTTP responses where the bridge advertises itself via favicon or redirect. Population is the headline number for this survey — direct internet-exposed self-hosted teleop bridges.

deployment_tells: Docker image foxglove/studio (the desktop renderer, less common) or osrf/ros:humble + foxglove_bridge launched as a ROS package
Launch file foxglove_bridge_launch.xml or foxglove_bridge_launch.py with port:=8765 the default
Co-deployed siblings on same IP (shadow-sweep priorities): rosbridge_server :9090, web_video_server :8080, Nav2/MoveIt action servers (via rosbridge), DDS UDP :7400+
Browser-side app at studio.foxglove.dev or self-hosted desktop client connects to ws://<host>:8765
Academic robotics labs: Foxglove is the de-facto teleop + data-review console across hundreds of public ROS2 GitHub repos
Startup deployments: drone, agriculture, last-mile delivery — Foxglove is the standard early-stage teleop UI
PX4-Autopilot and Isaac ROS reference stacks ship foxglove_bridge as a recommended companion package
Cert subject-CN patterns: teleop.<org>, ops.<org>, mission.<org>, foxglove.<org>, console.<org>
Often behind no reverse proxy at all — direct port 8765 in firewall rules is the typical pattern
Foxglove Cloud (paid SaaS, app.foxglove.dev) is a different product with OAuth — out of scope for this exposure class
pivot_paths: WebSocket /listChannels → topic-list enumeration (capability fingerprint of attached robot)
WebSocket /listParameters → parameter enumeration (often reveals robot model, map filename, costmap config)
First server-message after handshake → serverInfo JSON (name, version, capabilities)
Channel-list with /move_base*, /move_group*, /cmd_vel topics → confirms Nav2 + MoveIt are attached behind the bridge
Channel-list with /image_raw or /camera/* topics → confirms live camera feed is reachable
Channel-list with /tf, /tf_static → kinematic chain reveals robot model and joint structure
Shadow-sweep on same IP: 9090 (rosbridge), 8080 (web_video_server), 9091 (rosapi), UDP 7400+ (DDS direct)
TLS cert subject-CN on :443 or :8765 with TLS enabled → VisorGraph operator-portfolio pivot
do_not_call: WebSocket 'publish' message on any robot control topic — robot moves
WebSocket 'advertise' message creating a new publisher on a control topic — sets up the move primitive
WebSocket 'callService' on any state-changing service (clear_costmap, reset_localization, set_param)
WebSocket 'setParameters' message — modifies live ROS parameters
Subscribing to high-bandwidth topics (camera, lidar, pointcloud) without need — operator-visible bandwidth spike
Connecting and holding a session — increments the bridge's connection-count metric the operator sees
data_class: robot capability surface + live sensor stream (camera, lidar, IMU, joint state, costmap) when subscribed; primary harm is unauthenticated motion command via publish message (kinetic-impact safety hazard); secondary: live operator situational awareness leak (facility interior, fleet positions, ongoing tasks)
restraint_notes: Identity probe = WebSocket handshake only; read Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header and the first serverInfo frame; do not send subscribe
Channel list (/listChannels) is the read-only enumeration boundary at Stage 0c
Subscribing to data topics pulls live bandwidth and is operator-visible — channel list is sufficient at this stage
Never send publish, advertise, callService, or setParameters — any of these is the harm-side of the open-state finding
Connection itself increments the bridge's connection-count metric — keep sessions short; one handshake + listChannels + close is the discipline
Severity rationale: a Foxglove bridge exposing Nav2/MoveIt topics is remote-robot-control on the public internet; the open state is the headline finding
Foxglove Cloud (paid SaaS) is auth-on-default — only the self-hosted foxglove_bridge ROS package is in scope
Insight #40 watch-item: if foxglove_bridge ever adds a default token parameter, track which release fraction adopts it

version_history_auth_relevant.foxglove_bridge v0.5.x (2022): initial ROS package release; no auth; port 8765 default established
version_history_auth_relevant.foxglove_bridge v0.6.x (2023): TLS / certfile / keyfile params added — encryption only, not auth
version_history_auth_relevant.foxglove_bridge v0.7.x (2023-2024): ROS2 Iron / Jazzy compatibility improvements; no auth added
OAuth / org / role model — separate product, not the self-hosted bridge
version_history_auth_relevant.2026-06-09 status: no auth in self-hosted foxglove_bridge launch params
